claims.statement: Regulation (EU) 2024/886 requires the payer's PSP to offer verification before authorization and requires that verification service to be free to the payment-service user.
The verification obligation applies to euro standard and instant credit transfers; the deadline for PSPs in non-euro Member States, including Poland, is 9 July 2027.

Non-consumer bulk users may opt out, PSPs choose how to provide bulk verification, corporate systems must handle close-match, no-match and unavailable results, and the corporate remains liable for the authorized payment.

The EPC's published Verification of Payee API specification covers inter-PSP messages only, so an AP vendor needs a PSP, bank or authorized solution-provider interface rather than assuming direct scheme access.

SurePay already offers bulk APIs, a bank-branded corporate portal, audit logs and account-verification intelligence at substantial scale, directly overlapping the proposed workflow and data advantage.
AIB already gives bulk-payment customers a SurePay portal that returns per-payee results in downloadable CSV, demonstrating bank-controlled distribution of a native corporate workflow.

A public Bank Account Verification price card charges EUR 2,000 for 2,500 checks down to EUR 25,000 for 50,000 checks, establishing an upstream cost comparator but not enterprise willingness to pay for exception handling.

The EBA and ECB reported EUR 2.5 billion of fraudulent credit transfers in 2024 and that users bore about 85% of credit-transfer fraud losses, supporting real payment-fraud pain but not this product's conversion.

The EPC states that Verification of Payee is messaging functionality and cannot itself be relied on to identify a private or legal person, so an exception console must not treat a close match as identity proof.

contrary_evidence: SurePay already provides the bulk API, white-label portal, audit trail and shared verification intelligence proposed here.
AIB demonstrates that banks can distribute the corporate portal natively and retain the customer relationship.
The EPC API is inter-PSP only, making access to regulated responses partner-controlled.
The mandated verification is free to users and commodity APIs publish per-check pricing, limiting monetization of the check itself.
Corporate bulk users may opt out, and the corporate retains payment liability even after receiving a result.
Polish non-euro PSPs do not face the deadline until 9 July 2027 and the regulation concerns euro credit transfers.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: tenant-specific supplier-alias and evidence playbooks weighted by confirmed outcomes; no cross-tenant identity graph is assumed without explicit lawful permission
fingerprint.customer: euro-area enterprise AP teams and payment bureaus whose bank or AP platform exposes Verification of Payee results; Polish euro workflows become a later 2027 wedge
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: contracted AP-software, PSP and accounting-platform integrations that expose the payer's verification result
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: read-only exception console, beneficiary-evidence vault, supplier-master correction and human approval workflow; it neither performs the mandated verification nor releases funds
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: enterprise or AP platform pays a tenant subscription and documented-resolution fee, never a charge for the mandated PSP verification
fingerprint.problem_trigger: a payer's PSP returns close match, no match or verification unavailable before a euro credit transfer is authorized

founder_fit: Strong technical fit with finance, entity resolution, anomaly detection and auditable data workflows.
The founder can prototype a read-only console part-time, but bank-grade security, payments counsel and enterprise integration support must be delegated.

The UNVALIDATED HYPOTHESIS that capital_required_pln=95000 funds a controlled pilot fits the founder's own capital ceiling, but the lack of a PSP or AP relationship and the 2027 Polish timing weaken immediate founder access.
risks: A false or overconfident resolution can facilitate fraud or a misdirected payment.
The product could cross into regulated payment activity if it initiates, blocks or authorizes transfers rather than remaining read-only workflow software.
Payment, beneficiary and supplier-master data require bank-grade security, retention controls and incident response.
A bank, PSP or AP vendor can withhold the verification response or bundle the same exception workflow.
Cross-tenant alias learning may lack a legal basis, breach confidentiality or amplify poisoned supplier data.
A low exception rate may leave insufficient value beyond the free bank-provided result.

structure.commercial_archetype: PSP-authorized corporate beneficiary-exception workflow and evidence service
structure.control_point: enterprise AP approval queue after a PSP result and before a human authorizes the payment
structure.critical_dependency: a contracted PSP or AP-platform interface exposing verification results plus lawful access to the enterprise supplier master

thesis: Sell a read-only exception and evidence layer to euro-area enterprise AP teams only where a bank, PSP or AP platform contractually exposes the Verification of Payee result. After a close match, no match or unavailable result, the product gathers supplier-master, legal-name and trusted-contact evidence, recommends a supplier-record correction or escalation, and preserves an audit trail for a human approver; it never performs the mandated verification, treats a close match as identity proof, or releases funds. The initial moat is tenant-specific resolution history, not an assumed cross-enterprise alias graph. Direct bank and SurePay products make distribution and differentiation the central problem, while Poland is a later euro-flow market because its deadline is July 2027.
title: Verification-of-Payee Exception Network
uncertainties: Whether banks and AP platforms expose machine-readable verification results to an independent workflow vendor
Close-match, no-match and unavailable-result volume by enterprise and payment file
Enterprise willingness to pay beyond a bank-provided free result and portal
Permissible use and retention of supplier aliases, legal identifiers and resolution outcomes across tenants
Security certification, insurance, payments-law review and integration cost for a bank-grade pilot
Whether documented resolution reduces fraud or merely shifts manual work and liability
Partner sales cycle, churn, support burden and founder-compatible operating load
